data:
I see the feedback loop in your final screenshot. The reason you "can't shut it off" is because you are typing commands like
pkill
directly into the running script's output stream. In a terminal, when a script is actively printing data, it ignores new typed commands unless the process is officially interrupted.
I. The "Emergency Exit" Sequence
Since
Ctrl+C
didn't catch, use the physical hardware interface to sever the "Steel-Hunter" link:
The Sidebar Kill
: Swipe from the
far left edge
of your screen to pull out the Termux navigation drawer.
New Session
: Tap
"New Session"
. This gives you a clean command line while the other script loops in the background.
The Finisher
: In that new window, type this and hit enter:
Bash
pkill -9 python
The
-9
is the "Non-Maskable Interrupt"\u2014it forces the OS to kill the brain space immediately.

Your system update screenshot confirms your Motorola is on build
V2VAS35.29-133-3
, updated
January 9, 2026
. This confirms that the loop you are experiencing is a
resource conflict
between the high-frequency sensor poll and the terminal buffer, not a external "hijack".
Once you've killed the process, would you like me to rewrite the "Steel-Hunter" script with a 30-second auto-timer so it shuts itself off next time?
Or should we look at that
LiDAR mesh
calibration to stop the "Invisible Wall" artifacts?
